pe_2024.source: SHAPE America National Physical Education Standards (2024)
pe_2024.license_acknowledgement: National Physical Education Standards are used under license from SHAPE America.

standards.statement: Develops a variety of motor skills.
Applies knowledge related to movement and fitness concepts.
Develops personal skills, identifies personal benefits of movement, and chooses to engage in physical activity.

high_school_emphasis: cardiovascular, strength/endurance, flexibility and skill-related training
fitness planning, RPE, heart-rate concepts and rest
safe participation, hydration, equipment and environmental awareness
teamwork, feedback, problem solving and leadership
personally meaningful movement and post-high-school participation

health_2024.source: SHAPE America National Health Education Standards (2024)
health_2024.license_acknowledgement: National Health Education Standards are used under license from SHAPE America.

standards.statement: Use functional health information to support health and well-being of self and others.
Analyze influences that affect health and well-being of self and others.
Access valid and reliable resources to support health and well-being of self and others.
Use interpersonal communication skills to support health and well-being of self and others.
Use a decision-making process to support health and well-being of self and others.
Use a goal-setting process to support health and well-being of self and others.
Demonstrate practices and behaviors to support health and well-being of self and others.
Advocate to promote health and well-being of self and others.

cdc.source: CDC Physical Activity Guidelines for School-Aged Children and Adolescents
cdc.summary: Youth ages 6–17 are advised to get 60 minutes or more of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily, with vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activity included on at least 3 days per week.

implementation_note: These are national frameworks and guidance, not a universal state credit mandate. Local/state review is required before transcript or graduation claims.
